Hi all,

Operational summary (high level) — what we will run once we have the signed authorization and confirmed object list:

1) Lock: We pause new write activity to the CH-4821 tenant and snapshot active nodes (no customer-visible downtime beyond <1 minute orchestrated lock).
2) Identifier enumeration: Confirmed target buckets: s3://redwood-prod/ch-4821/prompts, /outputs/ch-4821/, /kv-cache/ch-4821/. We will also enumerate request logs from the ingest plane for the date range supplied.
3) Sweep job: A coordinated multi-stage sweep: prefix deletion + KV zeroization + index rebuild to force GC. Sweep runs on dedicated ops pool with immutable run id.
4) Evidence collection: Per-object deletion receipts (UUID), sweep summary CSV (counts, objects deleted, ops worker ids), and redaction proof (hash before/after for redacted columns).
5) Audit bundle: We will package 1) run metadata, 2) signed certificate, 3) sweep CSV, 4) scrub logs. Sensitive artifacts will be delivered via a time-limited Drive folder or SFTP at your preference.

Estimated time: 72 hours from authorization to completion for CH-4821 (historical depth up to 3 years). If you need same-day or expedited service there is a one-time ops surcharge and impacted SLA window.

Attachments: deletion_runbook_v2.pdf (internal ops runbook - redacted), sample_sweep_summary_template.csv

Karthik Iyer

Hi Julio — a couple security notes before we run:

- Proof formats: We will provide signed certificates (PDF) and a sweep_summary CSV. For additional assurance we can provide a notarized hash manifest for the deleted objects (good for your internal audit).
- Evidence retention: Redwood retains deletion-run metadata for 90 days strictly for internal audit and post-mortem; we can redact PII from any retention artifacts on request.
- Delivery: SFTP with two-factor key or shared Drive folder with tenant-scoped ACLs are both acceptable; please indicate which you prefer.

Please confirm an authorized signatory (name + role) and whether CloudHealth requires retention of any artifacts beyond the standard 90-day retention for evidence.
